messages:
ana: Quick heads-up — after the kernel selector change (prefer-fused-int8) I’m seeing p99 jump on small prompts in prod. p95 ~120ms unchanged, p99 from ~190ms -> ~320ms. Anyone else?
liam: saw the alert, yup. looks tied to requests <200 tokens. cc @sasha @kai
sasha: can you paste the profiler snippet you grabbed?
ana: (typo) pasted below — sample traces from the slow tail: 
```
2026-03-17T12:02:01Z TRACE req_id=... tokens=72 kernel=fused_int8 elapsed_ms=285 kv_cache_miss=1
2026-03-17T12:02:01Z TRACE req_id=... tokens=310 kernel=fp16_fast elapsed_ms=110 kv_cache_miss=0
2026-03-17T12:02:02Z TRACE req_id=... tokens=48 kernel=fused_int8 elapsed_ms=302 kv_cache_miss=1
```
liam: interesting — kv_cache_miss correlates with the slow ones. fused_int8 seems to hit a cold path + higher setup latency for tiny microbatches. :thinking:
sasha: also check batching knobs — our pool currently uses max_wait_ms=8 and max_batch_tokens=2048. small requests might be waiting, getting dispatched with microbatch shape that triggers fallback kernel.
kai: my read: fused kernel has better throughput for large batches but worse per-request init cost. for tiny microbatches the scheduler might pick the slower-but-warm fp16 or fallback path.
nana: ran a quick canary: set max_wait_ms=2 and max_batch_tokens=1024 on a 5% slice (us-west-1/g2). results: p99 dropped to ~210ms, p95 stable. posting infra-bot summary next.
infra-bot: canary job finished — p95=118ms, p99=212ms, throughput delta ~-2.3%. kv_cache_miss rate unchanged.
sasha: kv miss unchanged -> the tail might be kernel init / handoff cost rather than miss penalty. can you share kernel_selector logs?
nana: kernel selector snippet: 
```
kernel_selector: chosen=fused_int8 reason=tp_estimate(>threshold) fallback=none init_ms=45
kernel_selector: chosen=fp16_fast reason=batch_small fallback=kernel_init trigger_ms=180
```
liam: trigger_ms=180 is worrying — that's the observed init on that node. hedging/hand-off logic uses that to decide fallback, which explains spikes around ~180-300ms. we should decouple that from the hedging window and factor in request token count.
kai: propose experiment: enable kernel hedging for requests <150 tokens — spawn secondary dispatch to fp16 after 80ms if fused_int8 hasn’t responded. also try explicit KV priming for session hot keys.
sasha: + try prefer_warm_kernel flag and pre-warm the fused_int8 handles for the small-batch queue. might reduce init_ms.
nana: opened a PR with two config variants: A) reduce max_wait_ms to 2 + prefer_warm_kernel=true; B) keep max_wait_ms=8 but enable hedging to fp16 after 80ms. running A/B at 20/20/60 (A/B/control).
infra-bot: rollout started: A->20% nodes=g2pool-xx, B->20% nodes=g2pool-yy, control->60%.
liam: add scoped tracing for kernel_init time, hedged_dispatch latency, and kv_cache_priming hits. need p99 parity across regions before concluding.
sasha: FYI we hit a similar tail regression in 2025-11; root cause was kernel_init on fallback path — we fixed that by caching kernel handles and pre-warming. fused_int8 might have changed ABI so caching doesn't cover it yet.
kai: actionable: (1) ana collect trace samples + KV hit/miss histograms, (2) liam tweak scheduler knobs for small-token window, (3) sasha run warm_pool script for fused_int8 on canary nodes, (4) infra run canary 48h and collect p99/p95/throughput.
nana: noted — I'll push traces to /dashboards/perf-scan and update the thread with 24h numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
liam: +1. if we can get p99 <220ms with <3% throughput hit we can flip defaults. thanks team.
